q: 设计原则在 LLD 面试中的主要作用是什么？
q_en: What is the main role of design principles in an LLD interview?
scenario: 45 分钟停车场题，你刚画完类图，面试官追问「为什么这样拆类」而不是让你报术语。
scenario_en: Forty-five minutes into a parking-lot question, you've just drawn the class diagram and the interviewer asks why you split the classes that way, not to name terms.
options: 帮助你做类和抽象的取舍，并说清楚理由
要求你逐字背出每个原则的缩写
替代面试里的需求澄清环节
保证任何设计都必须足够复杂
options_en: They help you make and explain tradeoffs about classes and abstractions.
They require you to recite every acronym word for word.
They replace the requirements-clarification step.
They guarantee every design must be sufficiently complex.
why: 面试官更在意你是否用原则做出并解释好设计，而不是你能不能像背单词一样报出 SOLID。
why_en: Interviewers care whether you use design principles to make and explain good tradeoffs, not whether you can recite SOLID from memory.

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：SRP、OCP、LSP、ISP、DIP 五项面向对象设计原则的合称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, and Dependency Inversion.

optionExplanations: 对，因为面试官打分看的是你能不能用原则支撑设计决定，不是考记忆力。
误解：这不是背诵测验，死记缩写换不来任何设计判断分。
误解：澄清需求和运用设计原则是两件事，原则不能替你把范围问清楚。
误解：原则不是为了炫技堆复杂度，很多时候恰恰是用来砍掉不必要的复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — interviewers grade whether you can use principles to justify real decisions, not recite them.
Misconception: this isn't a memory quiz, reciting acronyms earns no design credit.
Misconception: clarifying requirements and applying principles are separate skills; principles can't do your scoping for you.
Misconception: principles aren't about showing off complexity — often they're the tool you use to cut it.

q: 如果只能优先记住三个通用软件设计原则，应该选哪三个？（多选）
q_en: If you could only prioritize three general software design principles, which three should they be? (multi-select)
scenario: 这场 LLD 面试只考单机对象建模，不涉及多副本一致性，你只能带三条通用原则进场。
scenario_en: This LLD round is pure single-process object modeling, nothing about replica consistency, and you can only bring three general principles in with you.
options: KISS
DRY
YAGNI
CAP 定理
options_en: KISS
DRY
YAGNI
the CAP theorem
why: KISS、DRY、YAGNI 覆盖复杂度、重复和过早设计三类常见问题；CAP 定理是分布式一致性话题，不是这篇 LLD 原则的重点。
why_en: KISS, DRY, and YAGNI matter most because they cover complexity, duplication, and premature design, while the CAP theorem belongs to distributed systems, not this LLD principles list.

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：优先选能工作的最简单方案，而不是炫技的复杂设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid, meaning you should prefer the simplest design that actually works.

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

termDefinitions.meaning: YAGNI（You Aren't Gonna Need It）：只实现当前需求真正要求的功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI stands for You Aren't Gonna Need It, meaning you should only build what current requirements actually need.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分布式系统里一致性、可用性、分区容忍性最多同时满足两项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says a distributed system can fully guarantee only two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

optionExplanations: 对，它管住过度设计冲动，逼你先选最简单能跑的方案。
对，它管的是重复逻辑分散在多处、改一处漏改另一处的风险。
对，它管住提前实现没人要的未来功能这个坑。
误选：CAP 讲的是分布式一致性/可用性权衡，属于系统设计话题，跟这三条 LLD 原则不是一类问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it keeps overengineering in check by forcing the simplest workable design first.
Correct — it targets logic scattered across places where fixing one spot but missing another causes bugs.
Correct — it stops you from building speculative future features nobody asked for.
Wrong pick: CAP is a distributed consistency/availability tradeoff from system design, not one of these three LLD habits.

scenario: 停车场题需求只要求停普通车、查空位，候选人却想引入五层工厂、装饰器和插件系统。
scenario_en: The parking-lot prompt only asks for parking a car and checking free spots, but the candidate wants five layers of factories, decorators, and a plugin system.
q: 面对这种过度设计冲动，哪个原则最该提醒他？
q_en: Which principle should rein in this urge to over-design?
options: Observer
KISS
分布式一致性
读写锁
options_en: the Observer pattern
KISS
distributed consistency
a read-write lock
why: KISS 要求先用能工作的最简单设计，复杂模式只有在简单设计撑不住真实变化时才加。
why_en: KISS says start with the simplest design that works and add complex patterns only once simplicity actually breaks down.
whenOtherWins: 如果 follow-up 明确要求多种可插拔计费或复杂扩展，再引入 Observer 等模式才合理。
tradeoff: 简单可行方案 vs 提前展示模式知识

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：优先选能工作的最简单方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid, meaning prefer the simplest design that works.

termDefinitions.meaning: Observer（观察者模式）：让订阅者在被观察对象状态变化时自动收到通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Observer pattern lets subscribers get notified automatically when an observed object's state changes.

optionExplanations: 跑题：Observer 是解决订阅通知的模式，用在这里只是提前展示模式知识，没有对应真实变化点。
对，先用能停车、能查空位的最简单设计，模式留到真的需要扩展时再加。
跑题：分布式一致性是多副本数据同步的话题，跟停车场这道单机题完全无关。
跑题：读写锁解决的是并发访问冲突，不是过度设计这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Off-target: Observer solves subscriber notifications; using it here is just flexing pattern knowledge with no real variation point.
Correct — start with the simplest design that parks a car and checks a spot, and add patterns only once real change demands it.
Off-target: distributed consistency is about syncing replicated data, unrelated to this single-machine parking prompt.
Off-target: a read-write lock solves concurrent access conflicts, not overengineering.

q: LLD 面试中过度设计最常见的坏处是什么？
q_en: What is the most common downside of overengineering in an LLD interview?
scenario: 候选人给 TicTacToe 套上工厂、策略、观察者三层模式，45 分钟里只剩 10 分钟写核心逻辑。
scenario_en: A candidate wraps TicTacToe in three layers of factory, strategy, and observer, leaving only ten of the forty-five minutes for the core logic.
options: 一定能拿到更高分
能自动满足所有未来需求
核心逻辑被模式层级淹没，还更难维护
会减少你解释设计的时间成本
options_en: It always earns a higher score.
It automatically satisfies every future requirement.
It buries the core logic under pattern layers and hurts maintainability.
It reduces the time you spend explaining the design.
why: 过多模式和层级会把简单问题变复杂；面试时间有限，复杂结构还会增加 bug 和沟通成本。
why_en: Too many patterns and layers bury simple logic, and with limited interview time the extra structure adds bugs and communication overhead.
optionExplanations: 误解：面试官看到的是不必要的复杂度，过度设计通常拉低分数而不是加分。
误解：模式堆再多也不会自动预判需求变化，往往还是猜错方向。
对，模式和层级一多，核心逻辑被埋起来，后面改动和沟通成本都更高。
误解：解释复杂结构反而更花时间，过度设计不会替你省时间。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: interviewers read unnecessary complexity as a red flag, not a bonus.
Misconception: stacking patterns doesn't magically predict future requirements — you often still guess wrong.
Correct — extra layers bury the core logic, making later changes and explanations more expensive.
Misconception: explaining a bloated structure eats more interview time, not less.

q: DRY 的真正关注点是什么？
q_en: What does DRY actually care about?
scenario: 折扣规则在下单和退款两处各写了一份，规则一改就必须同时改两处，漏一处就不一致。
scenario_en: The discount rule is written twice, once in checkout and once in refunds, so any rule change means editing both places or the two silently disagree.
options: 任何看起来相似的代码都必须立刻抽象
永远不能写两行相似的代码
所有类必须继承同一个父类
概念上相同的逻辑应该集中维护
options_en: Any code that looks similar must be abstracted immediately.
You must never write two similar-looking lines of code.
Every class must inherit from the same parent class.
Logic that is conceptually the same should be maintained in one place.
why: DRY 的价值是维护一致性：规则变了只改一处；文本相似但业务目的不同的代码不必强行合并。
why_en: DRY is about maintaining consistency so a rule change touches only one place, not about merging code that merely looks similar but serves different purposes.

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

optionExplanations: 误解：外表相似不等于同一个业务规则，硬抽象反而会把无关逻辑捆在一起。
误解：DRY 不是禁止任何相似代码，写两行像的代码本身不违反它。
误解：DRY 讲的是逻辑复用，不是要求所有类共享一个基类。
对，核心是同一条业务规则只维护一处，改动时不用到处找漏改的地方。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: looking similar isn't the same business rule — forcing an abstraction can bundle unrelated logic together.
Misconception: DRY doesn't ban any similar-looking code; writing two similar lines isn't a violation by itself.
Misconception: DRY is about logic reuse, not about forcing every class under one parent.
Correct — the point is one business rule lives in one place, so a change never gets missed somewhere else.

q: DRY 和 KISS 冲突时，成熟的回答应该是什么？
q_en: When DRY and KISS conflict, what does a mature answer sound like?
scenario: 相似逻辑刚出现第二次、需求还在变，面试官问要不要现在就抽一个公共基类出来。
scenario_en: The similar logic has only appeared a second time and the requirements are still moving, and the interviewer asks whether you would extract a shared base class right now.
options: 承认权衡：先简单，等重复稳定再抽象
永远立刻抽象
永远允许无限复制
只按代码行数决定要不要抽象
options_en: Acknowledge the tradeoff: stay simple first, abstract once duplication stabilizes.
Always abstract immediately.
Always allow unlimited duplication.
Decide purely by counting lines of code.
why: 强行抽象会制造人工耦合；说清楚“现在先简单，重复多处且概念相同时再提取”是更稳的判断。
why_en: Forcing an early abstraction creates artificial coupling, so the safer call is staying simple now and extracting only once the same-concept duplication is stable.
tradeoff: DRY 的集中维护 vs KISS 的当下简单

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：优先选能工作的最简单方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid, meaning prefer the simplest design that works.

optionExplanations: 对，先说清楚现在保持简单，等重复稳定出现、概念确实相同时再抽象。
误解：一看到相似就抽象容易制造人为耦合，抽早了比不抽更麻烦。
误解：放任无限复制会让规则改动时到处漏改，牺牲了 DRY 想保护的一致性。
误解：该不该抽象看的是概念是否相同，不是数代码行数这种表面指标。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — say plainly you'd stay simple now and extract only once the same-concept duplication is stable.
Misconception: abstracting the moment things look similar tends to create artificial coupling — too early is worse than none.
Misconception: letting duplication run wild means a rule change gets missed somewhere, losing the consistency DRY protects.
Misconception: whether to abstract depends on shared concept, not a surface metric like line count.

scenario: 题目没有提电动车、代客泊车或会员折扣，但候选人准备把这些全部实现。
scenario_en: The prompt never mentions EV charging, valet parking, or membership discounts, yet the candidate plans to implement all of them anyway.
q: 哪个原则最直接反对这种做法？
q_en: Which principle most directly argues against this approach?
options: CAS
YAGNI
LSP
Observer
options_en: CAS
YAGNI
LSP
the Observer pattern
why: YAGNI 是“现在不需要就别先建”；设计时可以留边界，但不要实现猜测中的未来功能。
why_en: YAGNI says not to build a feature before it is actually required, even though you can still leave clean seams for future extension.
whenOtherWins: 当面试官提出具体 follow-up（比如真的要支持电动车）时，再实现对应部分。
tradeoff: 当前需求的边界 vs 提前实现猜测中的未来功能

termDefinitions.meaning: YAGNI（You Aren't Gonna Need It）：只实现当前需求真正要求的功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI stands for You Aren't Gonna Need It, meaning only build what current requirements actually need.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAS（Compare-And-Swap）：一种无锁并发原语，先比较内存值再原子替换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAS stands for Compare-And-Swap, a lock-free concurrency primitive that atomically swaps a value only if it still matches an expected value.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能替换父类而不破坏承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle, meaning subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected.

termDefinitions.meaning: Observer（观察者模式）：让订阅者在对象状态变化时自动收到通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Observer pattern lets subscribers get notified automatically when an observed object's state changes.

optionExplanations: 跑题：CAS 是无锁并发原语，跟要不要提前实现未要求功能无关。
对，题目没要求电动车、代客泊车、会员折扣，现在就不该实现它们。
跑题：LSP 管子类能不能替换父类，不是在说该不该提前建功能。
跑题：Observer 是通知模式，跟这里的范围控制问题不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Off-target: CAS is a lock-free concurrency primitive, unrelated to whether to pre-build unrequested features.
Correct — the prompt never asked for EV charging, valet, or discounts, so none of them belong in the build yet.
Off-target: LSP is about subtype substitutability, not about whether to build ahead of requirements.
Off-target: Observer is a notification pattern, a different concern from scope control here.

q: “设计时考虑扩展”和“现在就实现未来功能”有什么区别？
q_en: What's the difference between designing with extension in mind and building future features now?
scenario: 停车场题只要求停普通车，你想先为未来的电动车充电留一个接口，面试官问这算不算 YAGNI。
scenario_en: The parking-lot prompt only asks for regular cars, you want to leave an interface for future EV charging, and the interviewer asks whether that is a YAGNI violation.
options: 两者含义完全相同，没有区别
前者禁止定义任何抽象接口
前者边界清晰，后者塞入非必要复杂度
后者实现总是比前者更简单
options_en: They mean exactly the same thing.
The former forbids defining any abstract interface.
The former keeps boundaries clean; the latter drags unnecessary complexity into the core design.
The latter is always simpler to implement.
why: 好设计可以为变化留清楚的接缝，但代码只实现当前需求，这样既不锁死未来，也不背负死功能。
why_en: A good design leaves clean seams for future change while the code itself implements only what is required today, avoiding both lock-in and dead features.
tradeoff: 为扩展留接缝 vs 现在就实现未要求的功能
optionExplanations: 误解：两者差别很大——一个只是留接口，一个是真的把未要求的功能写出来。
误解：留扩展空间不等于不能定义接口，恰恰经常需要一个干净的接口边界。
对，留接缝不写实现能保持边界干净，提前实现未要求功能只会背上死代码。
误解：现在就实现未来功能往往更费工夫，不见得比留接缝简单。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: they differ a lot — one just leaves a seam, the other actually ships an unrequested feature.
Misconception: leaving room to extend doesn't forbid interfaces — a clean interface boundary is often exactly the seam you leave.
Correct — leaving seams without implementing keeps boundaries clean, while building ahead just leaves dead code to maintain.
Misconception: building future features now is usually more work, not simpler than leaving a seam.

scenario: TicTacToe.play() 方法同时打印棋盘、读用户输入、更新棋盘状态、判断胜负。
scenario_en: A single TicTacToe.play() method prints the board, reads user input, updates board state, and checks for a winner all at once.
q: 这违反了什么原则？
q_en: Which principle does this violate?
options: CAS 原语
Singleton 模式
CAP 定理
关注点分离
options_en: the CAS primitive
the Singleton pattern
the CAP theorem
separation of concerns
why: 显示、输入和游戏规则是不同的变化原因，混在一个方法里会让测试、换 UI、改规则都变难。
why_en: Display, input, and game rules change for different reasons, so mixing them in one method makes testing, swapping the UI, and changing rules all harder.
whenOtherWins: 极小 demo 可以先写在一起，但面试设计应该展示清晰的职责边界。
tradeoff: 单方法的开发速度 vs 拆类后的可测试性

termDefinitions.meaning: CAS（Compare-And-Swap）：一种无锁并发原语。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAS stands for Compare-And-Swap, a lock-free concurrency primitive.

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton（单例模式）：保证一个类全局只有一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：一致性、可用性、分区容忍性最多同时满足两项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says a distributed system can fully guarantee only two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: Separation of Concerns（关注点分离）：把显示、输入、业务规则等不同变化原因拆到各自的类里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Separation of Concerns means responsibilities like display, input, and business rules should live in their own classes.

optionExplanations: 跑题：CAS 是并发原语，跟一个方法揽下显示、输入、规则判断无关。
跑题：Singleton 管的是全局唯一实例，不是这里职责混杂的问题。
跑题：CAP 定理是分布式系统的一致性权衡，这题只是一个单机方法设计问题。
对，显示、输入、规则是三个不同的变化原因，混一起会让测试和改动都变难。
optionExplanations_en: Off-target: CAS is a concurrency primitive, unrelated to one method owning display, input, and rules at once.
Off-target: Singleton is about a single global instance, not the responsibility-mixing problem here.
Off-target: the CAP theorem is a distributed-consistency tradeoff; this is a single-machine method design issue.
Correct — display, input, and rules change for different reasons, and mixing them makes testing and edits harder.

q: 把 Board、Display、InputHandler 拆开有哪些好处？（多选）
q_en: What are the benefits of splitting Board, Display, and InputHandler into separate classes? (multi-select)
scenario: TicTacToe 要求后续能从命令行换成 Web 界面，而且游戏规则必须能单独跑单元测试。
scenario_en: The TicTacToe design has to survive swapping the command line for a web UI later, and the game rules must be unit-testable on their own.
options: 让所有类互相知道对方的内部字段
可以单独替换输入方式
可以单独修改显示方式
可以独立测试游戏规则
options_en: It lets every class know the others' internal fields.
You can swap the input method independently.
You can change the display independently.
You can test the game rules independently.
why: 关注点分离让变化局部化；类之间不应通过暴露内部字段来协作。
why_en: Separating concerns localizes change, and classes should not collaborate by exposing their internal fields to each other.
diagram:
flowchart LR
I["InputHandler"] --> G["Game rules"]
G --> B["Board state"]
G --> D["Display/View"]
T["tests"] --> G
D --> U["UI output"]
optionExplanations: 误选：类之间不该通过暴露内部字段协作，拆分是为了减少这种耦合，不是增加。
对，输入方式可以单独替换，不用牵连显示或规则代码。
对，显示样式想改就改，不会碰到输入或游戏规则逻辑。
对，游戏规则能脱离真实输入和渲染单独跑测试。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong pick: classes shouldn't collaborate by exposing internal fields — splitting reduces that coupling, it doesn't add it.
Correct — you can swap the input method without touching display or rule code.
Correct — you can restyle the display without touching input or rule logic.
Correct — rules can be tested on their own, without real input or rendering.

q: Law of Demeter 主要想避免什么？
q_en: What is the Law of Demeter mainly trying to avoid?
scenario: 定价类靠 order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode() 取邮编算税，Address 一改它就跟着崩。
scenario_en: A pricing class calls order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode() to compute tax, so any change to Address breaks it too.
options: 穿透多层对象摸内部结构
所有方法调用
所有构造函数
所有接口
options_en: Reaching through multiple object layers to learn internal structure.
Every method call.
Every constructor.
Every interface.
why: 像 order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode() 这样的链式访问会让调用方耦合到三个对象的内部结构；更好的做法是在 Order 上提供更高层方法。
why_en: Deep chains like order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode() couple the caller to three objects' internals, so it is better to expose a higher-level method on Order instead.

termDefinitions.meaning: Law of Demeter（最少知识原则）：一个方法只应该和它的直接朋友对象交流，不穿透多层对象访问内部结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says a method should only talk to its immediate collaborators, not reach through layers of objects to access internal structure.

optionExplanations: 对，它反对调用方一路点下去摸清好几层对象的内部结构。
误解：LoD 不是反对方法调用本身，正常调用直接朋友对象完全没问题。
误解：LoD 跟构造函数无关，它管的是调用链穿透了几层对象。
误解：LoD 不反对定义接口，问题出在链式访问穿透内部结构。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it's against callers chaining through several layers of an object's internals.
Misconception: LoD doesn't oppose method calls in general — calling a direct collaborator is fine.
Misconception: LoD has nothing to do with constructors; it's about how many object layers a call chain crosses.
Misconception: LoD doesn't oppose defining interfaces; the problem is reaching through internals via chained calls.

q: 为什么 builder.setName(...).setAge(...).build() 通常不算 Law of Demeter 问题？
q_en: Why doesn't builder.setName(...).setAge(...).build() usually count as a Law of Demeter violation?
scenario: 评审说「链式调用超过两个点就违反 Law of Demeter」，你要判断 builder 的流式配置算不算。
scenario_en: A reviewer claims any chain with more than two dots violates the Law of Demeter, and you have to decide whether a fluent builder counts.
options: 因为链式调用永远安全
都在同一个构建器上连续设置，没有穿透其他对象
因为 Builder 模式不需要封装
因为它只存在于 Python 语言里
options_en: Because chained calls are always safe.
Every call stays on the same builder instance, so it never reaches through other objects' internals.
Because the Builder pattern doesn't need encapsulation.
Because it only exists in the Python language.
why: 问题不是点号数量，而是是否暴露并依赖多个对象的内部层级；流式接口通常在同一个抽象上连续配置。
why_en: The issue is not how many dots you chain, but whether you traverse multiple objects' internals, and a fluent builder keeps every call on the same abstraction.
tradeoff: 同一对象上连续配置 vs 穿透多个不同对象的内部结构

termDefinitions.meaning: Law of Demeter（最少知识原则）：只和直接朋友对象交流，不穿透内部结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says a method should only talk to its immediate collaborators, not reach through object internals.

termDefinitions.meaning: Builder（构造器模式）：用链式方法逐步设置字段，最后调用 build() 生成对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Builder pattern sets fields step by step through chained calls and produces the final object with a build() call.

optionExplanations: 误解：链式调用本身不天然安全，关键要看链条有没有穿透到别的对象内部。
对，builder 链式调用全程停留在同一个对象上，没有摸到其他对象的内部结构。
误解：Builder 模式照样需要封装，只是它把配置步骤留在同一个实例里。
误解：这是通用设计概念，不是某个语言独有的语法特性。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: chained calls aren't inherently safe — what matters is whether the chain reaches into other objects' internals.
Correct — every call in the builder chain stays on the same instance, never touching another object's internals.
Misconception: the Builder pattern still needs encapsulation; it just keeps configuration steps on one instance.
Misconception: this is a general design concept, not syntax unique to one language.

q: 补全 SOLID 五项：
q_en: Fill in the five SOLID letters:
why: 不必机械背诵，但要知道每项背后的设计判断。面试里更重要的是应用而不是报缩写。
why_en: SOLID stands for Single Responsibility, Open Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, and Dependency Inversion.

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：五项面向对象设计原则的合称，分别对应类职责、扩展方式、子类替换、接口粒度、依赖方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles covering class responsibility, extension, substitution, interface size, and dependency direction.

scenario: Report 类同时生成报告内容、格式化 PDF、还要把结果保存到文件。
scenario_en: A single Report class generates the content, formats it as PDF, and also saves the result to a file.
q: 最直接违反了什么原则？
q_en: Which principle does this most directly violate?
options: Actor
Observer
SRP
YAGNI
options_en: the Actor model
the Observer pattern
SRP
YAGNI
why: 内容生成、PDF 格式化、文件存储是三个不同的变化原因；拆成 Report、PDFPrinter、FileStorage 能让每类的变化互不牵连。
why_en: Content generation, PDF formatting, and file storage change for different reasons, so splitting them into Report, PDFPrinter, and FileStorage isolates each change.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是一次性脚本且不会扩展，简单函数也可能够用；面试里的可维护设计通常应该拆职责。
tradeoff: 单类的开发速度 vs 拆分后每个变化互不影响

termDefinitions.meaning: Actor（Actor 模型）：把并发单元建模成互相发消息、各自维护状态的独立实体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Actor model treats each concurrent unit as an independent entity that keeps its own state and communicates only via messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: Observer（观察者模式）：让订阅者在对象状态变化时自动收到通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Observer pattern lets subscribers get notified automatically when an observed object's state changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: SRP（Single Responsibility Principle）：一个类应该只有一个改变的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SRP stands for Single Responsibility Principle, meaning a class should have only one reason to change.

termDefinitions.meaning: YAGNI（You Aren't Gonna Need It）：只实现当前需求真正要求的功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI stands for You Aren't Gonna Need It, meaning only build what current requirements actually need.

optionExplanations: 跑题：Actor 模型管并发单元怎么互相发消息，跟这里的职责堆叠无关。
跑题：Observer 解决状态变化通知问题，不是这里三个职责混一个类的问题。
对，生成内容、排版 PDF、存文件是三个不同的变化原因，混一个类里最直接违反 SRP。
跑题：YAGNI 管该不该提前实现功能，这里的问题是职责混杂而不是范围过大。
optionExplanations_en: Off-target: the Actor model is about concurrent units messaging each other, unrelated to this responsibility pile-up.
Off-target: Observer solves state-change notification, not three responsibilities crammed into one class.
Correct — content generation, PDF formatting, and storage change for different reasons, the textbook SRP violation.
Off-target: YAGNI is about building ahead of requirements, not about responsibilities being tangled together.

q: 「一个类应该只有一个改变理由」描述的是哪项原则？
q_en: "A class should have only one reason to change" describes which principle?
scenario: CoffeeMachine 同时管库存和屏幕渲染，面试官说它「有好几个改变理由」，要你点名对应原则。
scenario_en: CoffeeMachine handles both inventory and screen rendering, the interviewer says it has several reasons to change, and asks which principle that names.
options: DIP
OCP
LSP
SRP
options_en: DIP
OCP
LSP
SRP
why: SRP 不代表类只能有一个方法，而是它的职责要凝聚，变化原因不能混杂。
why_en: SRP does not mean a class can only have one method — it means its responsibilities stay cohesive and its reasons to change do not mix.

termDefinitions.meaning: DIP（Dependency Inversion Principle）：高层业务应依赖抽象而不是具体实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP stands for Dependency Inversion Principle, meaning high-level logic should depend on abstractions.

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能替换父类而不破坏承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle, meaning subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected.

termDefinitions.meaning: SRP（Single Responsibility Principle）：一个类应该只有一个改变的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SRP stands for Single Responsibility Principle, meaning a class should have only one reason to change.

optionExplanations: 跑题：DIP 讲的是依赖抽象而不是具体实现，不是变化原因的数量。
跑题：OCP 讲的是扩展方式，不是一个类该有几个改变理由。
跑题：LSP 讲子类能不能替换父类，跟一个改变理由无关。
对，这正是 SRP 的定义：类的职责要凝聚，只对应一个变化原因。
optionExplanations_en: Off-target: DIP is about depending on abstractions, not the number of reasons to change.
Off-target: OCP is about how you extend behavior, not how many reasons a class has to change.
Off-target: LSP is about subtype substitutability, unrelated to one reason to change.
Correct — this is the literal definition of SRP: cohesive responsibility, one reason to change.

scenario: PaymentProcessor 用 if/elif 判断 credit、paypal 分支；每加一种支付方式都要改这个方法。
scenario_en: PaymentProcessor branches on payment_type with if/elif for credit and paypal, so every new payment method means editing this same method.
q: 更符合 OCP 的设计是什么？
q_en: Which design better follows OCP here?
options: 定义 PaymentMethod 接口，processor 只依赖接口
继续在 process() 里累加 if/elif 分支判断
把每种支付方式都写成模块级全局字符串
让上层 UI 组件直接跳过 processor 处理支付
options_en: Define a PaymentMethod interface so the processor depends on it, not branches.
Keep stacking if/elif branches inside process().
Turn every payment type into a module-level global string.
Let the UI layer skip the processor and handle payment itself.
why: OCP 希望新增行为通过新增实现类完成，而不是反复修改已验证过的旧代码；接口把变化点隔离出来。
why_en: OCP wants new behavior added through new implementation classes instead of repeatedly editing already-verified code, and the interface isolates the variation point.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有两种支付方式且以后不会扩展，简单分支可能更符合 KISS。
tradeoff: 扩展新支付方式的安全性 vs 引入接口的抽象成本

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：优先选能工作的最简单方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid, meaning prefer the simplest design that works.

diagram:

  +process(method,order)
}

  <<interface>>

}

optionExplanations: 对，PaymentMethod 接口把哪种支付方式的判断都挡在外面，新增方式只加实现类，不用碰 processor。
会一直越堆越长——每加一种支付方式就要重新触碰并测试这段已验证的分支逻辑。
只是换了个存储位置，字符串管不住行为差异，实际支付逻辑还得写在别处判断。
把支付逻辑甩给 UI 层只是转移问题，还破坏了本该由 processor 统一把关的职责边界。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a PaymentMethod interface keeps branching logic out of the processor, so adding a payment type only means writing one more class.
This keeps growing — every new payment method means reopening and retesting this already-verified branch logic.
Just relocates the string; it can't hold behavior differences, so the real logic still needs branching somewhere else.
Pushing payment logic to the UI only moves the problem and breaks the boundary the processor was meant to own.

q: OCP 的核心取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff of OCP?
scenario: 系统目前只有信用卡一种支付方式、半年没加过新的，面试官问现在抽 PaymentMethod 接口值不值。
scenario_en: The system has exactly one payment method today and has not added one in six months, and the interviewer asks whether extracting a PaymentMethod interface now is worth it.
options: 只适用于数据库场景
降低改旧代码风险，但需变化点明确
禁止创建任何新类
要求所有逻辑写进一个方法里
options_en: It only applies to database scenarios.
It lowers the risk of editing old code, but only once the variation point is clear.
It forbids creating any new classes.
It requires writing all logic into a single method.
why: 接口能让扩展更安全，但抽象本身有成本，只有变化点明确时才值得引入。
why_en: Interfaces make extension safer, but abstraction itself has a cost, so it only pays off once the variation point is real.
tradeoff: 回归风险降低 vs 抽象层的认知与维护成本

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

optionExplanations: 误解：OCP 是通用设计原则，不局限于数据库这一种场景。
对，接口能降低改旧代码的回归风险，但只有变化点确实存在时才值得付这份抽象成本。
误解：OCP 恰恰鼓励用新类扩展行为，不是禁止创建新类。
误解：把所有逻辑塞进一个方法正是 OCP 想避免的反模式。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: OCP is a general design principle, not limited to database scenarios.
Correct — interfaces lower the regression risk of editing old code, but that abstraction cost only pays off once change is actually happening there.
Misconception: OCP actually encourages extending behavior through new classes, not banning them.
Misconception: cramming all logic into one method is exactly the anti-pattern OCP tries to avoid.

scenario: Bird 基类定义了 fly()，Penguin 继承 Bird，但 fly() 里只能抛异常。
scenario_en: The Bird base class defines fly(), and Penguin extends Bird but its fly() can only raise an exception.
q: 这违反了什么原则？
q_en: Which principle does this violate?
options: DRY
Facade
LSP
YAGNI
options_en: DRY
the Facade pattern
LSP
YAGNI
why: 调用方以为任何 Bird 都能 fly，传入 Penguin 却破坏了这个承诺；基类不该承诺并非所有子类都能兑现的行为。
why_en: Callers assume every Bird can fly, but passing in a Penguin breaks that promise, so the base type should not guarantee behavior not every subtype can honor.
whenOtherWins: 如果基类只承诺 eat()，飞行能力单独放进 FlyingBird，Penguin 实现 Bird 就没问题。
tradeoff: 统一的 Bird 接口 vs 按能力拆分的子接口

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

termDefinitions.meaning: Facade（外观模式）：给一组复杂子系统提供一个更简单的统一接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Facade pattern provides one simplified interface in front of a set of complex subsystems.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能替换父类而不破坏承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle, meaning subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected.

termDefinitions.meaning: YAGNI（You Aren't Gonna Need It）：只实现当前需求真正要求的功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI stands for You Aren't Gonna Need It, meaning only build what current requirements actually need.

optionExplanations: 跑题：DRY 管重复逻辑，这里的问题是子类没法兑现父类承诺，不是代码重复。
跑题：Facade 是给复杂子系统包一层简化接口，跟继承承诺被打破无关。
对，调用方以为所有 Bird 都能 fly，Penguin 传进去却直接炸，正是 LSP 要防的问题。
跑题：YAGNI 管该不该提前实现功能，这里已经实现了 fly()，问题在承诺被破坏。
optionExplanations_en: Off-target: DRY is about duplicated logic; the problem here is a subtype that can't honor the parent's promise, not duplication.
Off-target: Facade wraps complex subsystems behind a simpler interface, unrelated to a broken inheritance promise.
Correct — callers assume every Bird can fly, and passing in a Penguin blows that up, exactly what LSP guards against.
Off-target: YAGNI is about building ahead of need; fly() already exists here, the issue is a broken promise.

q: LSP 在类层次设计中提醒你注意什么？
q_en: What does LSP remind you to watch for when designing a class hierarchy?
scenario: Square 继承 Rectangle 后，调用方开始写 instanceof 特判才能让面积计算跑对。
scenario_en: After Square extends Rectangle, callers start adding instanceof checks just to make the area calculation come out right.
options: 父类必须知道所有子类
子类必须覆写所有方法
继承永远优于组合
子类不能破坏父类的承诺
options_en: The base class must know about every subclass.
Subclasses must override every method.
Inheritance is always better than composition.
Subtypes must not break the promises the base type makes to callers.
why: 如果调用方需要 instanceof 特判，或子类方法抛“我不支持”，这条继承链通常已经出问题。
why_en: If callers need instanceof checks or a subclass throws an unsupported-method exception, the hierarchy is usually already broken.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能替换父类而不破坏承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle, meaning subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected.

optionExplanations: 误解：父类不需要知道有哪些子类，LSP 关心的是子类能不能替换它。
误解：子类不必覆写每个方法，只要不破坏父类的行为承诺就行。
误解：LSP 不是在比较继承和组合谁更好，它只管替换关系是否安全。
对，子类必须能在调用方眼里完全顶替父类，不能悄悄打破它承诺的行为。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the base class doesn't need to know its subclasses; LSP cares whether subtypes can substitute it.
Misconception: subclasses don't have to override every method, only avoid breaking the parent's behavior promise.
Misconception: LSP isn't judging inheritance versus composition, only whether substitution stays safe.
Correct — a subtype must fully stand in for its base type from the caller's view, without silently breaking a promised behavior.

scenario: Robot 被迫实现 eat() 和 sleep()，虽然机器人其实只会 work()。
scenario_en: Robot is forced to implement eat() and sleep(), even though a robot really only does work().
q: 更符合 ISP 的做法是什么？
q_en: Which approach better follows ISP here?
options: 拆成 Workable/Feedable 等小接口
让 Robot 的 eat() 空着不实现
在 eat() 里直接抛异常
把所有方法塞进一个巨大 Worker 接口
options_en: Split it into small interfaces like Workable and Feedable.
Leave Robot's eat() as an empty implementation.
Make eat() raise an exception directly.
Cram every method into one giant Worker interface.
why: ISP 反对胖接口；类只应该依赖和实现自己真正需要的能力。
why_en: ISP argues against fat interfaces — a class should only depend on and implement the capabilities it actually needs.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有实现确实都需要同一组方法，保留一个完整接口也可以。
tradeoff: 接口数量增多 vs 类不必实现无关方法

termDefinitions.meaning: ISP（Interface Segregation Principle）：接口应该小而专注。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ISP stands for Interface Segregation Principle, meaning interfaces should be small and focused.

optionExplanations: 对，拆成 Workable/Feedable/Restable 后，Robot 只实现 Workable，不用背无关能力。
空实现留着一个不会被用到的方法，调用方仍以为 Robot 支持 eat()，隐患没解决。
抛异常只是把接口不匹配的问题推迟到运行时才爆出来，接口本身还是太胖。
所有能力挤进一个 Worker 接口，Robot 照样被迫依赖它用不到的方法。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — splitting into Workable/Feedable/Restable lets Robot implement only Workable, no unrelated capability baggage.
An empty implementation still advertises eat() to callers who will assume it works — the hazard just moves, it doesn't disappear.
Throwing just defers the interface mismatch to runtime instead of fixing that the interface was too fat to begin with.
Jamming every capability into one Worker interface still forces Robot to depend on methods it never uses.

q: 胖接口通常会带来哪些坏味道？（多选）
q_en: Which code smells does a fat interface usually cause? (multi-select)
scenario: 一个 Worker 接口塞进了 eat()、sleep()、work()，Robot 类被迫把三个方法全部实现。
scenario_en: One Worker interface bundles eat(), sleep(), and work(), forcing the Robot class to implement all three.
options: 空实现
更清晰的职责边界
抛「不支持」异常的方法
类被迫依赖无关能力
options_en: empty implementations
clearer responsibility boundaries
methods that throw an unsupported exception
classes forced to depend on unrelated capabilities
why: 胖接口把无关职责绑在一起；小接口能按能力组合，减少虚假实现。
why_en: A fat interface bundles unrelated responsibilities together, while small interfaces compose by capability and avoid fake implementations.
optionExplanations: 对，胖接口逼类实现用不上的方法，只能留空充数。
误选：这是拆小接口后才有的好处，胖接口本身只会让边界更模糊。
对，用不上的方法只能抛不支持异常，把接口不匹配问题推给运行时。
对，类被迫依赖一堆跟自己无关的能力，耦合到没用的方法上。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a fat interface forces classes to implement methods they don't need, so they're left empty.
Wrong pick: that benefit only shows up after splitting into small interfaces; a fat one just blurs the boundary.
Correct — unusable methods end up throwing an unsupported-method exception, pushing the mismatch to runtime.
Correct — classes get stuck depending on capabilities that have nothing to do with them.

scenario: NotificationService 的构造函数里直接 new EmailSender，测试会真的发邮件，改 SMS 也要改这个服务。
scenario_en: NotificationService directly news up an EmailSender in its constructor, so tests send real emails and switching to SMS means editing this service.
q: 更符合 DIP 的设计是什么？
q_en: Which design better follows DIP here?
options: 把 EmailSender 做成全局变量
依赖 MessageSender 接口，构造函数注入实现
在 notify() 里加更多 if 判断渠道
让单元测试直接连接真实邮件服务
options_en: Turn EmailSender into a global variable.
Depend on a MessageSender interface, injected via the constructor.
Add more if-branches inside notify() for each channel.
Let unit tests connect to the real email service directly.
why: DIP 要求高层业务依赖抽象而不是具体实现；构造注入是实现 DIP 的常见技术，也顺带提升了可测试性。
why_en: DIP requires high-level logic to depend on an abstraction rather than a concrete class, and constructor injection is the common technique that also improves testability.
whenOtherWins: 非常简单且不会替换实现的脚本可以直接 new，但面试里的服务设计通常应该暴露依赖边界。
tradeoff: 直接 new 的简单性 vs 依赖抽象带来的可测试性

termDefinitions.meaning: DIP（Dependency Inversion Principle）：高层业务应依赖抽象而不是具体实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP stands for Dependency Inversion Principle, meaning high-level logic should depend on abstractions rather than concrete implementations.

optionExplanations: 全局变量只是换了个地方硬编码具体实现，测试照样绕不开真实的 EmailSender。
对，依赖 MessageSender 接口再从构造函数注入，测试可以换成假实现，换渠道也不用改这个服务。
每加一个渠道就多一个 if 分支，服务代码会越改越乱，跟依赖抽象的方向相反。
让单测连真实邮件服务会让测试变慢、不稳定，还是没有解开对具体实现的依赖。
optionExplanations_en: A global variable just relocates the hard-coded concrete sender; tests still can't avoid the real EmailSender.
Correct — depend on a MessageSender interface and inject it via the constructor, so tests swap in a fake and adding a channel skips this service.
Every new channel adds another if-branch, making the service messier — the opposite direction from depending on an abstraction.
Letting unit tests hit the real email service makes them slow and flaky, and still never breaks the concrete dependency.

q: DIP 和 dependency injection 的关系是什么？
q_en: What is the relationship between DIP and dependency injection?
scenario: 你说 OrderService 该依赖 PaymentGateway 接口，面试官追问「那和构造函数传实例是一回事吗」。
scenario_en: You say OrderService should depend on a PaymentGateway interface, and the interviewer asks whether that is the same thing as passing an instance into the constructor.
options: 依赖注入是原则，DIP 是 Python 语法
两者完全无关
DIP 是设计原则，依赖注入是实现它的常见技术
DIP 要求所有对象都必须是 Singleton
options_en: Dependency injection is the principle and DIP is Python syntax.
The two are completely unrelated.
DIP is the design principle, and dependency injection is a common technique for implementing it.
DIP requires every object to be a Singleton.
why: DIP 说的是依赖要指向抽象；DI 是通过构造函数、参数或容器把具体实现传进来的技术手段。
why_en: DIP says dependencies should point at abstractions, while DI is the technique of passing concrete implementations in via constructors, parameters, or a container.
tradeoff: DIP 定义“依赖什么” vs DI 提供“怎么传进来”

termDefinitions.meaning: DIP（Dependency Inversion Principle）：高层业务应依赖抽象而不是具体实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP stands for Dependency Inversion Principle, meaning high-level logic should depend on abstractions rather than concrete implementations.

termDefinitions.meaning: DI（依赖注入）：把对象依赖的具体实现从外部传入，而不是在内部自己创建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DI stands for Dependency Injection, a technique that passes an object's dependencies in from the outside instead of creating them internally.

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton（单例模式）：保证一个类全局只有一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

optionExplanations: 误解：两者都不是某种语言语法，DIP 是设计原则，跟 Python 没有绑定关系。
误解：两者关系很紧密，DI 正是落实 DIP 的常见手段，不是互不相干。
对，DIP 只规定该依赖抽象，DI 才是把具体实现从外部喂进来的注入手段。
误解：DIP 跟 Singleton 无关，它不要求任何对象必须是单例。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: neither is a language-specific syntax; DIP is a design principle with no tie to Python.
Misconception: they're closely related — DI is the common technique for implementing DIP, not something unrelated.
Correct — DIP just says point dependencies at an abstraction; DI is the injection mechanics that wire the concrete class in from outside.
Misconception: DIP has nothing to do with Singleton; it doesn't require any object to be a single instance.

q: 把用 OCP 重构支付处理的步骤排好：
q_en: Put these OCP-driven steps for refactoring payment handling in order:
steps: 新增 CreditCardPayment、PayPalPayment 等实现类
识别变化点是支付方式
让 PaymentProcessor 依赖 PaymentMethod 接口
新增 CryptoPayment 时不改 PaymentProcessor
why: 先找变化点，再抽象接口，最后通过新增实现扩展。这样才是为真实变化服务的 OCP。
why_en: OCP refactoring starts by identifying the payment variation point, introducing an interface, and adding implementations without changing the processor.
tradeoff: 先识别变化点再抽象 vs 直接一次性大重构

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

diagram:
flowchart TD
A["identify payment as variation point"] --> B["define PaymentMethod interface"]
B --> C["add concrete implementations"]
C --> D["processor calls abstraction"]
D --> E["new payment type adds class only"]

scenario: 类 A 调用 order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode() 来完成订单规则判断。
scenario_en: Class A calls order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode() just to run an order rule check.
q: 最直接可以怎么改？
q_en: What is the most direct fix here?
options: 把 zipCode 放进全局变量
让 A 直接继承 Address
把 Customer 和 Address 的字段都设为 public
让 Order 提供 getCustomerZipCode() 这样的高层方法
options_en: Put zipCode into a global variable.
Have A inherit directly from Address.
Make every Customer and Address field public.
Have Order expose a higher-level method like getCustomerZipCode().
why: 调用方不该知道对象内部的嵌套结构；让拥有聚合关系的对象提供贴近需求的方法，能直接降低耦合。
why_en: Callers should not need to know an object's internal nesting, so letting the aggregate owner expose a purpose-built method directly reduces coupling.
whenOtherWins: 简单 DTO 序列化场景里，浅层字段访问可能可以接受，但业务规则不应该这样穿透。
tradeoff: Order 承担导航逻辑 vs 调用方自己穿透对象图

termDefinitions.meaning: Law of Demeter（最少知识原则）：只和直接朋友对象交流，不穿透内部结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says a method should only talk to its immediate collaborators, not reach through object internals.

optionExplanations: 全局变量只是绕开了封装，数据的所有权和更新责任反而更难追踪。
让 A 继承 Address 建立了一个不成立的 is-a 关系，只为拿一个字段没必要绑死继承。
把字段全部公开等于放弃封装，任何调用方都能绕过 Order 直接改内部状态。
对，让 Order 提供 getCustomerZipCode() 这类高层方法，调用方就不用自己摸清对象内部结构。
optionExplanations_en: A global variable just bypasses encapsulation, making it harder to track who updates that data and when.
Having A inherit from Address creates a false is-a relationship just to reach one field — too heavy a coupling for that.
Making every field public gives up encapsulation entirely; any caller can now bypass Order and mutate internals directly.
Correct — Order exposing a higher-level method like getCustomerZipCode() keeps callers from reaching into internal structure.

scenario: 业务逻辑类里直接拼格式化字符串给 UI 展示，同时还在同一个方法里更新核心状态。
scenario_en: A business-logic class formats display strings for the UI directly, inside the very same method that also updates core state.
q: 更好的责任边界是什么？
q_en: What is a better responsibility boundary here?
options: 业务类管规则状态，展示交给 Display
把所有格式化逻辑都塞进数据库层
让 UI 层直接改业务状态字段
把核心状态字段整个删除掉
options_en: The business class owns rules and state; display owns formatting.
Push all formatting logic down into the database layer.
Let the UI layer edit business state fields directly.
Delete the core state fields entirely.
why: 展示变化和业务规则变化是不同的原因；拆开后 UI 改版不需要碰业务状态机。
why_en: Presentation changes and business-rule changes happen for different reasons, so separating them means a UI redesign never touches the business state machine.
whenOtherWins: 一次性命令行 demo 可以合并输出逻辑，但面试设计应该展示可维护的边界。
tradeoff: 合并输出的开发速度 vs 拆分后 UI 改版不影响业务状态
optionExplanations: 对，业务类只管规则和状态，格式化交给 Display 层，UI 改版不用碰状态机。
把格式化逻辑塞进数据库层只是换了个错误的地方，跟业务状态机还是绑在一起。
让 UI 层直接改业务状态字段等于跳过了业务规则的把关，容易写出不一致的状态。
直接删掉核心状态字段没解决职责边界问题，反而丢了业务本该记录的数据。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the business class owns rules and state, the display layer owns formatting, so a UI redesign never touches the state machine.
Pushing formatting logic into the database layer just moves it to the wrong place, still entangled with the business state machine.
Letting the UI edit business state fields directly skips the rule checks and invites inconsistent state.
Just deleting the core state fields doesn't fix the boundary problem — it loses data the business actually needs to track.

q: 在现代代码库里，应该如何看待 SOLID 原则的分量？
q_en: How much weight should SOLID carry in a modern codebase?
scenario: 一道 40 行代码就能答完的 TicTacToe 题，候选人为了凑齐 SOLID 五条加了五个接口。
scenario_en: On a TicTacToe question that fits in forty lines, the candidate adds five interfaces just to tick off all five SOLID letters.
options: 已经完全没有意义
仍然有用，但不该为套 SOLID 破坏 KISS
必须完整套用每一条，不能省略
只适用于系统设计面试，不适用于 LLD
options_en: It is completely meaningless now.
Still useful, but don't break KISS just to force-fit SOLID.
You must apply every single letter, no exceptions.
It only applies to system-design interviews, not LLD.
why: SOLID 来自继承和接口较重的时代；现在仍可用，但应该服务于问题，而不是制造不必要的复杂度。
why_en: SOLID comes from an era of heavy inheritance and interfaces, and it is still useful, but it should serve the problem rather than create unnecessary complexity.
tradeoff: SOLID 的结构清晰度 vs KISS 的当下简单

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：五项面向对象设计原则的合称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles.

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：优先选能工作的最简单方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid, meaning prefer the simplest design that works.

termDefinitions.meaning: LLD（Low-Level Design）：聚焦类、接口、对象交互的详细设计面试环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLD stands for Low-Level Design, the interview stage focused on classes, interfaces, and object interactions.

optionExplanations: 误解：SOLID 不是过时废案，很多判断（比如别把无关职责塞一个类）依然管用。
对，SOLID 仍然有用，但不该为了套全每一条而破坏 KISS，制造不必要的复杂度。
误解：机械套用每一条反而容易过度设计，SOLID 该服务于问题，不是打勾清单。
误解：SOLID 一样能用在 LLD 里的类和接口设计，不是系统设计专属。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: SOLID isn't obsolete — plenty of its calls, like not cramming unrelated responsibilities into one class, still hold.
Correct — SOLID is still useful, but you shouldn't break KISS just to force-fit every letter and add needless complexity.
Misconception: mechanically applying every letter tends toward overengineering; SOLID should serve the problem, not be a checklist.
Misconception: SOLID applies just as much to LLD class and interface design, it isn't exclusive to system-design interviews.

q: 哪些「场景 → 原则」映射是合理的？（多选）
q_en: Which "scenario → principle" mappings are reasonable? (multi-select)
scenario: 面试官列出四种代码症状，要你为每一种点名最直接对应的那条设计原则，错配会被追问。
scenario_en: The interviewer lists four code symptoms and wants you to name the one principle each maps to most directly, and a mismatch gets challenged.
options: 类混合多个变化原因 → SRP
新增类型总要改旧方法 → OCP
对象有很多可选参数 → Law of Demeter
子类不能支持父类方法 → LSP
options_en: A class mixes multiple reasons to change → SRP
Adding a new type always forces editing old methods → OCP
An object has many optional parameters → Law of Demeter
A subclass can't support a parent method → LSP
why: 很多可选参数更可能指向 Builder 或构造 API 的设计问题，不是 Law of Demeter。
why_en: Many optional parameters more likely point to a Builder or constructor-API design issue, not a Law of Demeter violation.
tradeoff: 对症选出正确的原则名称 vs 套用相近但不对的原则

termDefinitions.meaning: SRP（Single Responsibility Principle）：一个类应该只有一个改变的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SRP stands for Single Responsibility Principle, meaning a class should have only one reason to change.

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

termDefinitions.meaning: Law of Demeter（最少知识原则）：只和直接朋友对象交流，不穿透内部结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says a method should only talk to its immediate collaborators, not reach through object internals.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能替换父类而不破坏承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle, meaning subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected.

optionExplanations: 对，一个类混合多个变化原因，正是 SRP 要抓的信号。
对，新增类型总要改旧方法，说明变化点没被隔离，正是 OCP 该出手的地方。
误选：一个对象要传一堆可选参数，通常是该上 Builder 这类构造 API 的信号，不是调用链跑到别的对象内部。
对，子类没法支持父类承诺的方法，直接对应 LSP 被违反。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a class mixing multiple reasons to change is exactly the signal SRP flags.
Correct — a new type always forcing edits to old methods means the variation point isn't isolated, exactly where OCP applies.
Wrong pick: an object needing a stack of optional constructor args usually calls for a Builder-style API, not a caller reaching into another object's internals.
Correct — a subclass unable to support a promised parent method is a direct LSP violation.

scenario: 两个类都有相似的字符串格式化代码：一个是用户收据展示，一个是审计日志，两者的变化规则并不同。
scenario_en: Two classes have similar string-formatting code: one renders a user-facing receipt, the other writes an audit log, and their change rules differ.
q: 是否一定要马上抽成共享方法？
q_en: Do they have to be extracted into a shared method right away?
options: 必须放进父类
必须用 Singleton 统一管理
不一定；文本相似不等于概念相同，强抽可能耦合出错
一定要，因为 DRY 禁止任何相似代码
options_en: It must go into a parent class.
It must be centralized through a Singleton.
Not necessarily — similar text isn't the same concept, and forcing an abstraction can create the wrong coupling.
Yes always, because DRY forbids any similar-looking code.
why: DRY 看的是知识重复，不只是文本重复；不同业务目的的相似代码可以先分开，避免未来互相牵连。
why_en: DRY is about duplicated knowledge, not just duplicated text, so similar code serving different business purposes can stay separate to avoid entangling unrelated changes later.
whenOtherWins: 如果两处确实共享同一格式规范，并且会一起变化，抽出共同的 formatter 更合理。
tradeoff: 现在保持独立 vs 提前抽象共享逻辑

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton（单例模式）：保证一个类全局只有一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

optionExplanations: 误解：放进父类是继承层面的强绑定，跟两段代码要不要共享格式化逻辑是两码事。
误解：Singleton 管的是全局唯一实例，跟这两段格式化代码该不该合并无关。
对，文本相似不等于概念相同，收据展示和审计日志的变化规则不同，强行抽出来反而容易互相牵连。
误解：DRY 反对的是知识重复，不是禁止任何看起来相似的代码。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: putting it in a parent class is a heavy inheritance commitment, a different question from whether to share formatting logic.
Misconception: Singleton is about a single global instance, unrelated to whether these two formatting snippets should merge.
Correct — similar text isn't the same concept; the receipt and audit log change for different reasons, so forcing a merge risks entangling them later.
Misconception: DRY objects to duplicated knowledge, not to any code that merely looks similar.

q: 把应用设计原则的健康顺序排好：
q_en: Put the healthy order of applying design principles in sequence:
steps: 选择最小能解决当前问题的结构

why_en: Healthy principle use starts from real requirements and variation points, then adds only the abstraction needed.

B --> C{"repetition, coupling, or change pain?"}

scenario: OrderService 的方法里直接创建 StripeAPI 实例，导致单元测试必须连上真实的支付服务。
scenario_en: OrderService methods create a StripeAPI instance directly, so unit tests end up hitting the real payment service.
q: 哪项原则和技术最能改善这里的测试性？
q_en: Which principle and technique would most improve testability here?
options: 把所有字段都设成 public 属性
让 StripeAPI 反过来继承 OrderService
直接把相关单元测试删掉
用 DIP 依赖注入 PaymentGateway 接口
options_en: Make every field public.
Have StripeAPI inherit from OrderService instead.
Just delete the relevant unit tests.
Apply DIP and inject a PaymentGateway interface.
why: 依赖抽象之后，测试可以注入 fake 或 mock；业务逻辑不再绑死某个具体的外部服务。
why_en: Once the dependency points at an abstraction, tests can inject a fake or mock and the business logic is no longer tied to one concrete external service.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是一次性脚本，直接调用具体 API 也可能够用；面试里的服务设计通常应优先保留可测边界。

optionExplanations: 把字段全设成 public 只是放弃封装，测试照样得连真实的 StripeAPI。
让 StripeAPI 反过来继承 OrderService，关系完全颠倒，也没解决测试要连真实服务的问题。
删掉测试等于放弃验证，不是解决测试性问题的办法。
对，用 DIP 依赖 PaymentGateway 接口再注入，测试就能换成 fake，不用碰真实支付服务。

Deleting the tests means giving up verification, not fixing the testability problem.

q: 每加一种支付方式都要改 PaymentProcessor，最大的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest risk of editing PaymentProcessor every time a payment method is added?
scenario: PaymentProcessor 已上线跑着信用卡和 PayPal，现在加 Apple Pay 还得改同一段 if/elif。
scenario_en: PaymentProcessor is already live handling credit cards and PayPal, and adding Apple Pay still means editing that same if/elif block.
options: 反复改核心逻辑，增加回归 bug 风险
新增的实现类数量变得太少
接口的数量会变得太多太杂
自动化测试变得完全不需要
options_en: Repeatedly editing core logic raises regression-bug risk.
You end up creating too few new implementation classes.
You end up with too many, too scattered interfaces.
Automated testing becomes completely unnecessary.
why: OCP 想避免的正是稳定代码被反复打开修改；把变化放进新的实现类能缩小回归范围。
why_en: OCP exists precisely to avoid reopening stable code again and again, and pushing change into new implementation classes shrinks the regression surface.

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

optionExplanations: 对，反复打开这段核心逻辑改，每次都可能牵连出新的回归 bug。
误解：问题不是实现类太少，恰恰是没有用新实现类去承接变化。
误解：这里根本没引入接口，也就谈不上接口数量太多太杂。
误解：反而应该加测试防回归，自动化测试不会因此变得不需要。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — reopening this core logic every time risks pulling in a new regression bug each round.
Misconception: the problem isn't too few implementation classes, it's that new classes aren't being used to absorb the change at all.
Misconception: no interface was introduced here, so there's no interface-sprawl problem to speak of.
Misconception: if anything you need more regression tests here — automation doesn't become unnecessary.

scenario: CoffeeMachine 类同时管理库存、收款、冲泡配方和屏幕渲染，后续每个新需求都要改它。
scenario_en: CoffeeMachine manages inventory, payment, brew recipes, and screen rendering all at once, so every new requirement means editing it.
q: 你会如何解释重构方向？
q_en: How would you explain the refactoring direction here?
options: 把所有方法都统一改成 static 方法
按变化原因拆成四个协作类分开管理
只在原有方法里继续叠加 if 分支判断
只把类的名字换一个就足够
options_en: Turn every method into a static method.
Split into four collaborating classes by reason to change.
Keep stacking if-branches inside the original method.
Just rename the class and call it done.
why: SRP 不是为了类的数量多，而是让库存、支付、配方、显示的变化互不牵连。
why_en: SRP isn't about having more classes — it's about keeping inventory, payment, recipe, and display changes from tangling with each other.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目只要求最小冲泡流程、不涉及支付和显示，先留一个简单 orchestrator 也可以。
tradeoff: 单类快速起步 vs 拆分后每个变化互不影响
diagram:
flowchart LR
CM["CoffeeMachine orchestrator"] --> I["Inventory"]
CM --> P["Payment"]
CM --> R["Recipe/Brewer"]
CM --> D["Display"]
I --> IR["stock changes"]
P --> PR["payment changes"]
R --> RR["brew rules"]
D --> DR["UI text"]
optionExplanations: 把方法都改成 static 只是换个调用方式，库存、支付、配方、显示还是缠在一起变化。
对，按变化原因拆成库存、支付、配方、显示四个协作类，各自改动互不牵连。
继续叠 if 分支只会让这一个类越来越臃肿，职责混杂的问题完全没解决。
只改名字不改结构，库存、支付、配方、显示还是绑在同一个类里一起变化。
optionExplanations_en: Turning every method static just changes how it's called; inventory, payment, recipe, and display still change together.
Correct — split by reason to change into inventory, payment, recipe, and display classes so each change stays isolated.
Stacking more if-branches only bloats this one class further, leaving the tangled responsibilities untouched.
Renaming the class without restructuring it still leaves inventory, payment, recipe, and display bound together.

q: 为什么「接口越多越好」不是正确理解 SOLID？
q_en: Why is "more interfaces is always better" a wrong reading of SOLID?
scenario: 45 分钟的 LLD 题里，候选人给每个类都配了接口，包括永远只会有一个实现的 Board。
scenario_en: In a forty-five-minute LLD question the candidate gives every class an interface, including Board, which will only ever have one implementation.
options: 接口这种语法只能用在 Java 语言里
接口在任何场景下都完全没有成本
接口也有认知成本，只有真实变化点才值得加
接口会自动帮你生成对应的实现代码
options_en: Interfaces only exist as a Java-only syntax feature.
Interfaces never carry any cost in any scenario.
Interfaces have cognitive cost too, so they're worth adding only at a real variation point.
Interfaces automatically generate their implementations for you.
why: 抽象能隔离变化，但也会增加间接层；面试里要展示你知道何时加、何时不加。
why_en: Abstraction isolates change but also adds a layer of indirection, so the interview signal is knowing when to add it and when not to.
tradeoff: 接口带来的扩展安全 vs 额外的间接层认知成本

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：五项面向对象设计原则的合称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles.

optionExplanations: 误解：接口是通用的面向对象概念，不是 Java 独有的语法。
误解：接口不是零成本的，多一层间接就多一层要理解和维护的东西。
对，接口也有认知成本，只有真的存在变化点时才值得为它多加一层间接。
误解：接口不会自动生成实现，该写的实现类一个都少不了。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: interfaces are a general OO concept, not Java-only syntax.
Misconception: interfaces aren't free — every extra layer of indirection is one more thing to understand and maintain.
Correct — interfaces carry cognitive cost too, worth the extra indirection only when a real variation point exists.
Misconception: interfaces don't auto-generate implementations; you still have to write every implementing class.

q: 关于如何在面试里使用这些设计原则，哪些说法是合理的？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about using these design principles in an interview are reasonable? (multi-select)
scenario: 候选人每讲一句就点名一条 SOLID，面试官却一直追问「那你为什么这样拆类」。
scenario_en: The candidate names a SOLID letter in every sentence, while the interviewer keeps asking why the classes were split that way.
options: 不需要不断点名原则
用原则指导决策并解释取舍
原则是思考工具，不是打勾清单
必须在每句话里都提一次 SOLID
options_en: You don't need to keep naming principles out loud.
Use principles to guide decisions and explain tradeoffs.
Principles are thinking tools, not a checklist to tick off.
You must mention SOLID in every single sentence.
why: 好的设计会自然体现原则；刻意报术语不如清楚说明为什么这样拆类或抽象。
why_en: Good design shows the principles naturally, so explaining why you split a class or added an abstraction beats reciting the term names.

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：五项面向对象设计原则的合称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles.

optionExplanations: 对，好设计会自然体现原则，不需要嘴上反复点名字。
对，原则该用来支撑你的决策并解释取舍，这才是面试官想听的。
对，原则是帮你判断的思考工具，不是拿来打勾交差的清单。
误选：刻意在每句话里塞 SOLID 只会显得在背书，不会加分。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — good design shows the principles naturally, no need to keep naming them out loud.
Correct — principles should back up your decisions and explain the tradeoff, that's what interviewers want to hear.
Correct — principles are thinking tools for judgment calls, not a checklist to tick off.
Wrong pick: forcing SOLID into every sentence just reads as reciting, it earns no extra credit.

scenario: 面试官问：“为什么不现在就抽象出一个 Validator 服务？”
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: "Why not abstract out a Validator service right now?"
q: 哪个回答最成熟？
q_en: Which answer sounds the most mature?
options: 因为 DRY 原则从来都不重要
我会立刻抽象出所有校验逻辑
Validator 必须做成 Singleton 模式
现在只有 User 一处用，先放 User 里；多处重复再提取
options_en: Because the DRY principle never matters.
I would abstract all validation logic immediately.
Validator must be built as a Singleton.
Only User uses this today, so keep it there for now and extract once the rule repeats in multiple places.
why: 这个回答同时体现了 KISS、DRY 和 YAGNI 的平衡；没有拒绝抽象，只是把它推迟到有证据时再做。
why_en: This answer balances KISS, DRY, and YAGNI at once — it doesn't reject abstraction, it just defers it until there's real evidence for it.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求已经写明多个实体共享同一验证规则，提前抽出 Validator 就合理。
tradeoff: 现在保持简单 vs 提前抽象共享校验逻辑

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton（单例模式）：保证一个类全局只有一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

optionExplanations: 误解：这否定了 DRY 的价值，实际上答案本身也在用 DRY 的判断，只是不着急动手。
立刻抽象所有校验逻辑是在没有证据前先下重注，只有多个实体已经共享规则时才该这样做。
误解：Validator 该不该做成 Singleton 是另一个问题，跟现在要不要抽象没关系。
对，现在只有 User 用，先放着；等重复出现在多处再提取，同时兼顾了 KISS、DRY、YAGNI。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: this dismisses DRY entirely, but the right answer is still using DRY's judgment call, just not rushing it.
Abstracting all validation immediately bets early without evidence — that only makes sense once multiple entities already share the rule.
Misconception: whether Validator should be a Singleton is a separate question, unrelated to whether to abstract it now.
Correct — only User uses it today, so keep it there and extract once the rule repeats elsewhere, balancing KISS, DRY, and YAGNI.

scenario: 团队已有的 EmailSender 只提供 sendHtmlEmail(subject, body, ccList)，而 NotificationService 的业务需要只是「发出一条消息」。
scenario_en: The existing EmailSender only offers sendHtmlEmail(subject, body, ccList), while all NotificationService's business logic needs is "deliver one message".
q: DIP 里的「倒置」倒置的到底是什么？
q_en: In DIP, what exactly is being inverted?
options: 倒置的是调用方向：低层模块反过来调用高层模块的方法
接口按高层业务的需要定义，实现反过来适配它
倒置的是继承方向：让具体类当抽象类的父类
倒置的是创建时机：把 new 推迟到第一次真正使用时
options_en: The call direction is inverted: low-level modules call into high-level ones.
The interface is defined by what the high-level business logic needs, and implementations adapt to it.
The inheritance direction is inverted: concrete classes become parents of abstract ones.
Creation timing is inverted: the constructor call is deferred to first real use.
why: 正常情况是业务迁就实现，被迫按 sendHtmlEmail 那套参数走；DIP 让业务先定义 send(message)，实现来适配。代价是这层抽象要由业务侧承担。
why_en: Normally the business bends to whatever the implementation offers; DIP flips it so the business defines send(message) first and implementations adapt — the price is that the business side now owns that abstraction.

termDefinitions.meaning: DIP（Dependency Inversion Principle）：高层业务依赖抽象，而不是依赖具体实现类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP stands for Dependency Inversion Principle: high-level logic depends on an abstraction rather than a concrete implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: abstract class（抽象类）：只声明方法签名、由子类补上实现的基类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An abstract class declares method signatures and leaves subclasses to supply the implementations.

optionExplanations: 误解：DIP 不改运行时谁调用谁，业务照样调发送方；变的是接口由谁定形状。
对，先按 NotificationService 的需要把签名定成一个参数，具体发送方再来实现这个签名。
误解：继承方向没有变，EmailSender 仍然是抽象的子类，不会反过来当父类。
误解：推迟创建是懒加载的话题，跟接口由谁定义无关。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: DIP doesn't change who calls whom at runtime; it changes who defines the interface's shape.
Correct — the signature is fixed to one parameter to suit NotificationService, and the concrete sender implements that signature.
Misconception: the inheritance direction is unchanged; EmailSender stays a subtype of the abstraction.
Misconception: deferring construction is lazy loading, unrelated to who defines the contract.

scenario: Bird 基类有 fly()，Penguin 覆写后抛 NotImplementedError，调用方于是开始写 instanceof 特判绕开企鹅。
scenario_en: The Bird base class has fly(), Penguin overrides it to raise NotImplementedError, and callers start writing instanceof checks to route around penguins.
q: 这个类层次该怎么改？
q_en: How should this class hierarchy be reshaped?
options: 在 Bird.fly() 里加 canFly 标志位，飞不了的子类就直接返回
把 fly() 下沉到 FlyingBird，Penguin 仍继承 Bird
让 Penguin 不再继承 Bird，把 Bird 的整套行为复制一份进去
在调用方维护不会飞的鸟名单，每次调 fly() 前先查一次表
options_en: Add a canFly flag inside Bird.fly() so flightless subclasses just return early.
Push fly() down into FlyingBird, leaving Penguin on Bird.
Stop letting Penguin extend Bird and copy Bird's whole behavior into it.
Keep a list of flightless birds on the caller side and check it before every fly() call.
why: 「会飞」是能力差异而不是运行时状态，把它下沉到 FlyingBird 后每个 Bird 子类都能兑现承诺。代价是多一层类型，所有声明 Bird 却调 fly() 的地方都要改。
why_en: Flight is a capability difference, not a runtime flag; pushing fly() down into FlyingBird lets every Bird subtype honor its promise, at the cost of one more type and rewriting callers that typed on Bird but called fly().
whenOtherWins: 如果所有子类其实都能飞、只是飞法不同，fly() 就该留在 Bird 上，不需要拆出 FlyingBird。
tradeoff: 层次扁平（方法都放基类）vs 契约诚实（能力分层）

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能在父类出现的地方顶替它，不破坏父类的承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle: a subtype must stand in wherever the base type is expected without breaking its promises.

termDefinitions.meaning: instanceof（类型判断）：运行时检查一个对象到底是哪个具体子类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An instanceof check asks at runtime which concrete subclass an object actually is.

termDefinitions.meaning: abstract class（抽象类）：只声明方法签名、由子类补上实现的基类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An abstract class declares method signatures and leaves subclasses to supply the implementations.

codeSample:
class Bird(ABC):
    def eat(self) -> None: ...

class FlyingBird(Bird):      # 只有会飞的那一支才有 fly
    def fly(self) -> None: ...

class Sparrow(FlyingBird): ...
class Penguin(Bird): ...     # 不再被迫实现 fly，也不用抛异常
optionExplanations: 标志位把契约问题挪进了运行时：调用方仍会拿到一个「答应会飞却不飞」的对象，静默失败比抛异常更难查。
对，只有真的会飞的子类才实现 fly()，Bird 的每个子类都能替换基类，instanceof 特判自然消失。
断开继承会丢掉 eat() 等共享行为，复制一份鸟的逻辑又违反 DRY，改一处要改两处。
名单只是把 instanceof 特判换了个存放地点，调用方依然要知道具体子类是谁。
optionExplanations_en: A flag pushes the contract problem into runtime: callers still get an object that promised flight and silently does nothing.
Correct — only genuinely flying subtypes implement fly(), every Bird subtype substitutes cleanly, and the instanceof checks disappear.
Cutting inheritance loses shared behavior like eat(), and copying the bird logic repeats it in two places to maintain.
A lookup list just relocates the special-casing; callers still need to know which concrete subtype they hold.

scenario: 停车场的 Vehicle 层次里 Car、Motorcycle、Truck 都要计费，只有 ElectricCar 需要 startCharging()，需求没提别的车充电。
scenario_en: In the parking lot's Vehicle hierarchy, Car, Motorcycle, and Truck all get billed, but only ElectricCar needs startCharging(), and no other vehicle charges.
q: startCharging() 该声明在哪一层？
q_en: At which level should startCharging() be declared?
options: 放 Vehicle 基类，非电动车的实现里抛 UnsupportedOperation
放 Vehicle 基类，非电动车实现成什么都不做的空方法
只放在 ElectricCar 这一支上，Vehicle 不声明它
放 Vehicle 基类，调用前用 instanceof 判断是不是电动车
options_en: Put it on Vehicle and have non-electric vehicles throw UnsupportedOperation.
Put it on Vehicle and have non-electric vehicles implement it as a no-op.
Declare it only on the ElectricCar branch; Vehicle never mentions it.
Put it on Vehicle and instanceof-check for electric cars before calling.
why: 判据是基类上的每个方法必须所有子类都能真正兑现；充电只有电动车能兑现，放上去就会逼出空实现或特判。代价是调用方要先拿到 ElectricCar 类型。
why_en: The test is that every base-class method must be genuinely honorable by all subtypes; only electric cars can honor charging, so hoisting it forces no-ops or special cases — the cost is callers must first hold an ElectricCar.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求改成每辆车都要上报能耗，那这个方法就属于所有子类，应该声明在 Vehicle 基类上。
tradeoff: 基类统一签名（调用方省事）vs 基类只承诺人人做得到的事

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能在父类出现的地方顶替它，不破坏父类的承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle: a subtype must stand in wherever the base type is expected without breaking its promises.

termDefinitions.meaning: ISP（Interface Segregation Principle）：接口要小而聚焦，别逼类实现它用不到的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ISP stands for Interface Segregation Principle: keep interfaces small and focused so classes aren't forced to implement methods they never use.

termDefinitions.meaning: instanceof（类型判断）：运行时检查一个对象到底是哪个具体子类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An instanceof check asks at runtime which concrete subclass an object actually is.

optionExplanations: 抛异常是 LSP 的经典红旗：任何拿着 Vehicle 的代码都可能在运行时炸，编译期看不出来。
空实现让摩托车「假装充上电了」，用户以为在充电其实没有，是比报错更隐蔽的故障。
对，充电只属于电动车这一支，Vehicle 就不该承诺它，调用方也不会被诱导去调。
特判把类型知识散到每个调用点，以后新增一种可充电车型要回头改所有判断处。
optionExplanations_en: Throwing is the classic LSP red flag: any code holding a Vehicle can blow up at runtime with nothing visible at compile time.
A no-op makes a motorcycle pretend it charged — the user thinks charging started when nothing happened, a quieter failure than an error.
Correct — charging belongs to the electric branch only, so Vehicle shouldn't promise it and callers are never tempted to call it.
Special-casing scatters type knowledge across call sites, so a second chargeable vehicle type means revisiting all of them.

scenario: 重构后 NotificationService 的构造函数收一个 MessageSender 接口，EmailSender 实现这个接口，两者不再互相 new。
scenario_en: After the refactor, NotificationService takes a MessageSender interface in its constructor and EmailSender implements it; neither constructs the other.
q: 重构后两个模块的依赖关系变成什么形状？
q_en: What shape does the dependency between the two modules take after this refactor?
options: NotificationService 依赖 EmailSender，EmailSender 再依赖那个接口
高层和低层都依赖 MessageSender 接口，彼此不知道对方存在
EmailSender 反过来依赖 NotificationService，方向整个掉头
接口依赖两个实现类，两个实现类之间也互相引用
options_en: NotificationService depends on EmailSender, which in turn depends on the interface.
Both the high-level and low-level module depend on the MessageSender interface and neither knows the other exists.
EmailSender now depends on NotificationService, reversing the direction entirely.
The interface depends on both implementations, which also reference each other.
why: 两侧都指向同一个抽象，换成 SMS 实现时 NotificationService 一行不用改，测试也能塞假实现。代价是接口本身成了要维护的契约，改签名两边都得动。
why_en: Both sides point at the same abstraction, so swapping in SMS needs zero edits to NotificationService and tests can inject a fake — the cost is the interface becomes a contract you must maintain, and changing it touches both sides.

termDefinitions.meaning: DIP（Dependency Inversion Principle）：高层业务依赖抽象，而不是依赖具体实现类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP stands for Dependency Inversion Principle: high-level logic depends on an abstraction rather than a concrete implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: abstract class（抽象类）：只声明方法签名、由子类补上实现的基类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An abstract class declares method signatures and leaves subclasses to supply the implementations.

optionExplanations: 这还是重构前的形状：业务只要还握着具体的 EmailSender，就换不掉实现也测不了。
对，高层和低层同时指向 MessageSender，谁都不需要认识对方的类名。
误解：DIP 不是把依赖箭头调头，而是让两条箭头都指向中间的抽象。
误解：抽象不认识它的实现类，实现之间也没有引用关系，否则解耦就白做了。
optionExplanations_en: That's the pre-refactor shape: while the business still holds a concrete EmailSender, you can neither swap nor test it.
Correct — both modules point at MessageSender and neither needs to know the other's class name.
Misconception: DIP doesn't flip the arrow around; it makes both arrows point at the abstraction in the middle.
Misconception: the abstraction knows nothing about its implementations, and implementations don't reference each other.

scenario: 停车场题的计费只有两种：按小时计费和固定日票，需求里没有第三种，也没提运行时可插拔。
scenario_en: Parking-lot billing has exactly two modes today — hourly and a flat day pass — with no third mode and no runtime pluggability in the requirements.
q: 第一版计费逻辑该怎么写？
q_en: How should the first version of the billing logic be written?
options: 先搭 PricingStrategy 接口和两个实现类，为未来第三种计费铺路
用一个 if/else 分支处理这两种计费
用 factory 加配置文件在运行时组装计费规则
把每种计费做成插件，启动时动态加载进来
options_en: Build a PricingStrategy interface plus two implementations to pave the way for a third mode.
Handle both modes with a single if/else branch.
Assemble billing rules at runtime from a factory plus a config file.
Make each billing mode a plugin loaded dynamically at startup.
why: 两个分支的条件语句已经能跑通全部需求，strategy 的收益要等计费种类真的开始增长才兑现。代价是第三种计费到来时要回头做一次重构。
why_en: A two-branch conditional already covers every stated requirement, and the strategy pattern only pays off once billing modes actually multiply — the cost is one refactor when the third mode shows up.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求已经列出五种以上计费，或要求上线后不重启就能加规则，一开始就上 strategy 更划算。
tradeoff: 现在少写两个类和一个接口 vs 将来一次重构的成本

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：先用能工作的最简单方案，撑不住了再加复杂度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid: start with the simplest thing that works and add complexity only when simplicity stops working.

termDefinitions.meaning: strategy pattern（策略模式）：把一族可互换的算法各自包成一个类，运行时按需挑一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The strategy pattern wraps each of a family of interchangeable algorithms in its own class so you can pick one at runtime.

termDefinitions.meaning: factory（工厂模式）：把对象的创建过程集中到一个专门的类里，调用方不直接 new。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A factory centralizes object creation in a dedicated class so callers never call the constructor directly.

optionExplanations: 两个实现类加一个接口，换来的可扩展性目前没有需求兑现，是提前下注。
对，两种计费用一个条件语句就完整覆盖了需求，简单还撑得住就不加结构。
配置文件驱动组装引入了解析和校验两条新的出错路径，为两种固定计费付这个代价不值。
动态加载要处理加载失败和版本兼容，是给「上线后加规则」准备的，本题没有这条需求。
optionExplanations_en: Two implementation classes plus an interface buy extensibility no current requirement cashes in — that's betting early.
Correct — one conditional fully covers both modes, and while simplicity holds you don't add structure.
Config-driven assembly adds parsing and validation as new failure paths, too steep a price for two fixed modes.
Dynamic loading means handling load failures and version skew; it serves "add rules after deploy", which nobody asked for here.

scenario: 那个原本两分支的计费类现在有 500 行、混了十种职责，加一种支付方式要同时改五个地方。
scenario_en: That once two-branch billing class is now 500 lines with ten mixed responsibilities, and adding a payment method means editing five places at once.
q: 这时候该继续保持单类还是动刀？
q_en: At this point, keep the single class or restructure it?
options: 继续加分支：KISS 要求保持简单，就不该拆这个类
把分支抽成 strategy，按职责拆开这个类
保留这个类，给每个分支补上详细注释和文档
等真的出线上事故之后再决定要不要重构
options_en: Keep adding branches — KISS says stay simple, so this class should not be split.
Extract the branches into strategies and split the class by responsibility.
Keep the class as is and add thorough comments and docs to each branch.
Wait for a production incident before deciding whether to refactor.
why: KISS 的意思是简单还撑得住时不加复杂度；单类膨胀到十种职责、改一处要动五处，正是简单撑不住的两个具体信号。代价是拆分本身要花时间。
why_en: KISS means don't add complexity while simplicity still holds; ten responsibilities in one class and a change touching five places are the two concrete signals that it no longer does — and the split itself costs time.
whenOtherWins: 如果这个类还只有两三个分支、加一种计费只改一处，那不动它仍然是对的选择。
tradeoff: 维持单类的简单 vs 拆分换来的改动隔离

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：先用能工作的最简单方案，撑不住了再加复杂度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid: start with the simplest thing that works and add complexity only when simplicity stops working.

termDefinitions.meaning: strategy pattern（策略模式）：把一族可互换的算法各自包成一个类，运行时按需挑一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The strategy pattern wraps each of a family of interchangeable algorithms in its own class so you can pick one at runtime.

optionExplanations: 把 KISS 当成「永远别拆」是误读：它管的是何时开始加复杂度，不是禁止加。
对，职责膨胀和改一处动五处这两个信号同时出现，说明重构的收益已经兑现了。
注释解释不了为什么改一个功能要动五个地方，结构问题写文档只是记录痛苦。
等事故再动手意味着修复要在压力下做，而且此时这个类通常又长了一截。
optionExplanations_en: Reading KISS as "never split" misses the point: it governs when to start adding complexity, not whether you ever may.
Correct — responsibility bloat plus a change touching five places means the payoff from restructuring has arrived.
Comments can't explain away why one feature change touches five places; documenting a structural problem just records the pain.
Waiting for an incident means refactoring under pressure, by which point the class has usually grown further.

scenario: 停车场题只要求普通车位，候选人提前做了可插拔的 ChargingStation 抽象；后来真正来的新需求是「残障车位预约」。
scenario_en: The parking-lot prompt only asked for regular spots, but the candidate pre-built a pluggable ChargingStation abstraction; the requirement that actually arrived was "reserve accessible spots".
q: 这段提前写的充电抽象最终带来什么后果？
q_en: What does that pre-built charging abstraction end up costing?
options: 它可以直接复用到预约需求上，只要把类名和字段重命名一下
形状对不上新需求，却仍是要读、要编译、要维护的死代码
它会让预约功能的实现自动变快
它只增加代码行数，不产生维护成本
options_en: It can be reused for reservations directly, just by renaming the class and its fields.
Its shape doesn't fit the new requirement, yet it's still code to read, compile, and maintain.
It automatically makes the reservation feature faster to implement.
It only adds line count and creates no maintenance cost.
why: 提前建的抽象是按猜测的形状建的，猜错方向后新需求用不上它，它却还留在代码库里被读被测。这就是 YAGNI 说的代价：死代码不会自己消失。
why_en: A pre-built abstraction is shaped by a guess, and once the guess misses, the new requirement can't use it while it still sits in the codebase being read and tested — that's YAGNI's cost: dead code doesn't remove itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: YAGNI（You Aren't Gonna Need It）：只实现当前需求，不提前实现猜测中的未来功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI stands for You Aren't Gonna Need It: build what today's requirements need, not features you only guess you'll need later.

termDefinitions.meaning: abstract class（抽象类）：只声明方法签名、由子类补上实现的基类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An abstract class declares method signatures and leaves subclasses to supply the implementations.

optionExplanations: 充电和预约的状态模型完全不同——一个管电流会话，一个管时间段占用，改名换不来复用。
对，猜错形状后它既接不上新需求，也没人敢删（可能有代码在依赖），只剩维护负担。
误解：一段和新需求无关的抽象不会加速实现，反而多一处要读懂的代码。
误解：死代码要参与编译、跑测试、每次重构都被牵动，成本不止是行数。
optionExplanations_en: Charging and reservations model different state — one a current session, the other a time-slot hold — so renaming buys no reuse.
Correct — with the shape guessed wrong it fits nothing new, yet nobody dares delete it, leaving pure maintenance burden.
Misconception: an abstraction unrelated to the new requirement doesn't speed anything up; it's one more thing to read.
Misconception: dead code compiles, runs in tests, and gets dragged along by every refactor — the cost exceeds line count.
